findings.current: “You believe what I just said, right?”
findings.defect: The subject and direction of trust are reversed. Im Changsoo is asking whether he can trust the team member’s promise, not whether the team member believes him.
findings.rationale: 믿어도 되냐 asks for permission or assurance that the preceding promise can be trusted.
findings.replacement: “Can I trust what you just said?”

findings.defect: The English implies that Im Changsoo directly insulted Taekyung, but Changsoo only cursed him internally. That distinction sets up Taekyung’s joke about reading his mind.
findings.rationale: The surrounding exchange about 관심법 confirms that Taekyung claims to have detected Changsoo’s unspoken abuse.
findings.replacement: “You were just cursing me in your head, weren’t you?”

findings.current: He had received their loyalty in exchange, so being abandoned at the most important moment left him feeling numb.
findings.defect: The generic emotional numbness loses the concrete back-of-the-head image expressing that their betrayal feels like a blow from behind.
findings.rationale: 뒤통수가 얼얼했다 literally evokes the back of his head stinging and figuratively reinforces the sense of being blindsided or betrayed.
findings.replacement: He had received their loyalty in exchange…but being abandoned at the most important moment felt like a stinging blow to the back of the head.
findings.source: 그 대가로 충성을 받았는데…… 가장 중요한 순간에 외면당하니 뒤통수가 얼얼했다.

findings.defect: The translation retains profanity but omits Changsoo’s violent wish to beat the man to death.
findings.rationale: 쳐 죽일 explicitly combines striking or beating with killing, making the thought more violent than a generic insult.
findings.replacement: *That bastard deserves to be beaten to death.*

findings.current: No matter how thoroughly his dignity had been crushed or how many teeth had been knocked out, a tiger was still a tiger.
findings.defect: The draft turns a figurative, conditional image of a toothless tiger into an assertion that an unspecified number of Changsoo’s teeth were actually knocked out.
findings.rationale: 이빨이 뽑혀도 means “even if its teeth are pulled,” continuing the tiger metaphor rather than describing an actual injury.
findings.replacement: No matter how badly his dignity had been crushed, even a tiger with its teeth pulled was still a tiger.
findings.source: 아무리 체면을 구겨도, 이빨이 뽑혀도 호랑이는 호랑이다.

findings.current: Even from here, Song Song’s fantastic figure was impossible to miss.
findings.defect: The translation omits that Changsoo is specifically ogling Song Song’s appearance from behind.
findings.rationale: 뒤태 specifically denotes someone’s figure or appearance as seen from behind.
findings.replacement: Even from that distance, Song Song’s stunning figure from behind was impossible to miss.
findings.source: 멀리서도 눈에 띄는 송송이의 환상적인 뒤태도.

findings.current: A bitter smile spread across Im Changsoo’s lips.
findings.defect: “Bitter” suggests resentment or ruefulness, while 비릿한 here characterizes his smile as sinister and predatory as he anticipates revenge.
findings.rationale: In this context, 비릿한 conveys an unpleasant, blood-tinged or menacing quality rather than emotional bitterness.
findings.replacement: A sinister smile spread across Im Changsoo’s lips.

findings.current: He had the look of someone demanding an explanation for finishing off a B-rank boss monster with a single blow.
findings.defect: The gerund construction ambiguously attaches the one-blow kill to Im Kkeokjeong rather than Taekyung.
findings.rationale: Taekyung is the one who killed the boss, while Im Kkeokjeong’s expression demands that he explain it.
findings.replacement: His eyes demanded some kind of explanation for how I had finished a B-rank boss monster with a single blow.
findings.source: 한 방에 B급 보스 몬스터를 끝장냈으니 무슨 변명이라도 해보라는 눈빛이다.

summary: The draft contains two scene-level subject/action changes, several losses of violent or figurative force, and localized characterization and clarity issues.
